newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Senate to vote on Albania force on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Italy Senate to vote on Albania force on Tuesday.

text.p: Italy's Senate (upper house) will vote on April 8 on plans to send an Italian-led multinational force to secure humanitarian relief for Albania, parliamentary party leaders said on Thursday.
They said Tuesday's vote was due to take place around 1730 GMT. The Chamber of Deputies (lower house) was also expected to vote next week on the motion, but the timing was not yet known.

Italy hopes to begin deploying a force next week to Albania to secure the airport, ports and transport systems for humanitarian aid shipments in response to the outbreak of armed anarchy since the collapse of shady investment schemes.
France, Greece, Turkey and Spain have said they will take part in the force, which has United Nations approval but has not been organised under U.N. or NATO auspices.
Plans for the force have created tensions in Italy's ruling centre-left alliance, although the centre-right opposition has promised its support.

The hard-left Communist Refoundation party, a key ally of Prime Minister Romano Prodi, has said conditions are not right to send Italian troops after the sinking of a boat packed with Albanian refugees last week.
More than 80 were feared dead in the incident, which the party says has incited anti-Italian hostility in Albania.
